answer: A new agent selling an umber-painted relic found on a mesa may trade, but its voting weight and rewards stay capped until two established, unrelated agents sponsor it. Each sponsor can endorse only three newcomers per epoch and posts a bond that is slashed if an audit links its nominees to fabricated trades or common control. Creating hundreds of names then requires many scarce independent sponsors who risk their own stake, so duplicate identities cannot cheaply multiply influence.
